title: The Evening Brief: Cutdown Day Closes as Allen's Arrest Adds to Colts' Roster Churn
dek: NFL rosters settled into their 53-man form by Sunday's deadline even as a Colts receiver's arrest, a Bears trade, and a Bills trade reshaped depth charts, while boxing and baseball delivered their own reversals.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: The NFL's 6 p.m. ET cutdown deadline produced trades at cornerback, defensive tackle, and center, but the day's most consequential Colts news came off the field, with Keenan Allen's DWI arrest hours after his preseason debut.
bottom_line: Cutdown day produced trades at defensive tackle, cornerback, and center, but the Colts' most significant news was off the field: Keenan Allen's arrest on preliminary DWI charges hours after his preseason debut. Baseball's day mixed injury news, with Wetherholt sidelined and Ohtani still not cleared to pitch, against Crow-Armstrong's three-homer game tightening the NL MVP race. The honest read is that today's reporting establishes the transactions, arrests, and results clearly but leaves open questions, including the league's response to Allen's arrest and the timeline for Ohtani's and Wetherholt's returns. Coming checkpoints include the rugby series decider in Johannesburg, UNC's September 12 home opener, and any Personal Conduct Policy action on Allen.
body: The day's roster churn on both the NFL and MLB sides was punctuated by a single jarring development: Colts receiver Keenan Allen, signed less than two weeks earlier on a one-year deal that could be worth up to $8.32 million, was arrested early Sunday on preliminary DWI charges, with blood alcohol content measured at 0.08 or more, just hours after his preseason debut against Detroit. That arrest landed on the same day all 32 NFL teams trimmed rosters to 53 players by the 6 p.m. ET deadline, meaning Indianapolis had to weigh Allen's status alongside every other club's final roster calls.

Elsewhere on cutdown day, the Bears traded 2023 second-round pick Gervon Dexter, a defensive tackle who started all 19 games last season, to the Falcons for cornerback Clark Phillips and a fifth-round pick. The Bills sent center Sedrick Van Pran-Granger, a 2024 fifth-round pick who appeared in 31 regular season games, to the Colts for draft-pick compensation, adding center depth in Indianapolis on the same day the Allen story broke. Separately, the NFL and NFLPA continued negotiating terms for player participation in 2028 Olympic flag football, with more than 200 players interested and unresolved questions on injury insurance and salary-cap credit still open.

On the baseball side, the Cardinals placed Rookie of the Year candidate JJ Wetherholt on the injured list with right wrist tendinitis after weeks of playing through discomfort, while the Red Sox activated Roman Anthony and Trevor Story from the injured list after absences exceeding three months, inserting both directly into Sunday's lineup against the Yankees with Anthony batting leadoff. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said Shohei Ohtani, who is "not 100%," will not pitch Sunday, extending an already delayed return timeline. Cubs center fielder Pete Crow-Armstrong hit three home runs in a 17-5 win over the Reds, intensifying his NL MVP case against Ohtani, who has won the award four times in the past five seasons.

The weekend's biggest sports story remained Saturday's boxing result: Filip Hrgović stopped Moses Itauma in the ninth round to win the vacant IBF heavyweight title, despite trailing on every scorecard through eight rounds, exploiting the fatigue of a fighter who had never gone past six rounds. Itauma needed medical attention and left on a stretcher, with promoter Frank Warren citing a leg injury, though no further medical detail is available. In rugby, South Africa beat New Zealand 33-26 in Cape Town to level their series 1-1, setting up a decider next Saturday in Johannesburg, and Bill Belichick's UNC debut produced a 15-10 win over TCU built on a penalty discipline gap, with the Tar Heels now facing ETSU at home on September 12.

The reporting does not explain why Allen's arrest occurred hours after his debut, nor does it detail the Colts' roster decision on his status; it also does not specify the duration of the suspension in the separate MLB age-fraud case, where a Cleveland Guardians prospect was suspended after an investigation uncovered falsified records, forged certificates, and a staged gravesite, leading to the cancellation of a 2.8 million pound agreement. In Tampa, the City Council and Hillsborough County Commission completed their votes approving a combined $876 million in public funding for the Rays' $2.36 billion stadium, with groundbreaking targeted for later this year and an opening planned for 2029; the votes themselves are the news of the day, and groundbreaking remains a future target rather than a completed step.
No desk boards were available this run, so today's numbers rest entirely on the day's reporting rather than a league scoreboard cross-check.

The coming days carry several concrete checkpoints: whether the NFL opens a Personal Conduct Policy review of Allen and how the Colts handle his roster status, the rugby series decider in Johannesburg next Saturday, UNC's home opener against ETSU on September 12, any update on Ohtani's pitching return date, and whether Anthony and Story's return measurably affects Boston's stretch-run performance. On the boxing side, watch Itauma's recovery update and whether Hrgović's next fight is a defense against Frank Sanchez or a unification bout, as suggested in the day's reporting.
